quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the posted speed limit.
Follow the car in front of you very closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on your driving. Do not take other drivers' actions personally. Plan enough time for your trip, follow speed limits, and be patient with other drivers on the road.

questions.question: What should you do when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: Brake hard.
Keep your speed the same.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: When another vehicle is passing you, keep your speed steady. Do not speed up. Let the other vehicle pass safely and merge back into your lane.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to see how far away cars are and how fast they are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see how far away cars are and how fast they are going.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because of low visibility. You can only see as far as your headlights reach. This makes it difficult to judge the distance to other vehicles and their speeds.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, you should look to your:

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left and right for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from your left side will be closer to you. Also check across the entire intersection to make sure the path is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A yield sign is ahead.
A side road is entering from the left.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a yield sign is coming. Begin to slow down when you see this sign.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm?

options.text: Stop.
Go slowly at 15 mph if you do not see children.
Drive at normal speed but watch for children.

questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when you see a school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm. Stay stopped until the arm moves back and the bus starts moving again. This rule applies whether you are going the same direction as the bus or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What turn is this bicyclist signaling?

options.text: A left turn.
An upcoming stop.
A right turn.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand and arm signals to show other drivers what they plan to do. When a bicyclist extends their left arm straight out, they are signaling a left turn.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?

options.text: There is construction work ahead.
You must change lanes ahead.
There is a detour ahead.

questions.explanation: Orange signs warn of construction areas. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Areas where your vision gets blurry when you are tired.
Areas on the road that you cannot see in your mirrors.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas on the road that you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to go. Check near the rear corners of your vehicle for other cars. These areas are called blind spots because your mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, what should you do?

options.text: You must stop for them.
You do not have to stop for them.
You should honk your horn at them.

questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Even if they are jaywalking or crossing where they should not, you must still stop for them.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off the road. It is the most common cause of traffic crashes. Distractions make you miss important signs and sounds that help you avoid accidents.

questions.question: What should you do if you see animals near the road?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and drive carefully.
Swerve quickly into the next lane.

questions.explanation: Slow down and drive carefully when you see animals near the road. They may suddenly jump or change direction. There may be other animals out of sight nearby as well.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a safe driving practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic should stay in the right lane.
Change lanes without using your turn signal.
If you miss your exit, drive to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without using your turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes. Stay in the right lane if you are driving slower than other traffic. If you miss your exit, continue to the next exit. Do not back up or make U-turns on interstate highways.

questions.question: How is drowsiness similar to alcohol and drugs while driving?

options.text: It makes you a better driver.
It makes you feel better.
It impairs your judgment.

questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: What is a driving distraction?

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A driving distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen at any time and in any place. They can cause crashes that result in property damage, injury, or death.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: When you are tired, you may fall asleep while driving and crash. This can injure or kill you or others. Fatigue makes you slower at making decisions and increases your crash risk.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Sharp turn to the right ahead.
Upcoming sharp left and right turns.
Winding road ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road curves ahead. Slow down to a safe speed.

questions.question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, you should:

options.text: Press down hard on the accelerator.
Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.
Set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: Before you stop, check your mirrors to see what is around you. Release the accelerator and let your car slow down. Then press the brake pedal smoothly.

questions.question: If you drive more slowly than the flow of traffic, you will most likely:

options.text: Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.
Improve traffic flow.
Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.
questions.explanation: If you drive too slowly and block traffic, you may get a ticket. Drive at the same speed as other traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: As the percentage of alcohol (BAC) in your blood increases, you become:

options.text: More intoxicated.
More sober.
More coordinated.

questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if the path is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if the path is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can go. Let any cars or pedestrians in the intersection pass first. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When should drivers adjust their mirrors, seats, and steering wheels?

options.text: Before turning on their vehicles.
While backing out of their driveways.
Before reaching speeds of 55 mph or above.

questions.explanation: Adjust your seat, mirrors, and steering wheel before you start the engine. Also check that your brakes and turn signals work.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: Clear all your windows and mirrors before you drive. You need to see clearly in all directions.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
questions.explanation: In work zones, stay far away from other cars, barriers, equipment, and workers. Do not follow too closely behind other vehicles.

questions.question: Traffic control devices in work zones are the color:

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Be extra careful when you see these.

questions.question: It is unlawful to:

options.text: Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone.
Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not pass in no passing zones. Do not pass at railroad crossings, street crossings, or where solid yellow lines are next to your lane. Do not pass in work zones.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
There is two-way traffic.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic moves in both directions on this road.

questions.question: If you are feeling fatigued while driving, you should:

options.text: Increase your speed to reach your destination more quickly.
Increase the volume of your radio.
Find a safe parking area to take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe parking area to take a short nap.
questions.explanation: If you are struggling to stay awake, drifting out of your lane, or using the radio to stay awake, stop at a safe place and rest. A short nap will help you drive safely.

questions.question: What is an important step in turning?

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Increase your speed.
Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Before you turn, look behind you and to both sides of your car to make sure it is safe. Slow down to turn safely.

questions.question: When approaching a person using a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is well away from your path of travel.
Honk your horn as you proceed past them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is well away from your path of travel.
questions.explanation: Stop your car and wait until the person crosses and is safely away. Always give the right-of-way to blind pedestrians.
